source.title: Mean Mode Screaming: Mean-Variance Split Residuals for 1000-Layer Diffusion Transformers

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Reports deep-network training failures and stabilization in diffusion Transformers, extending the setting beyond the classification networks named in the versions; its generative training outcomes do not test those versions’ classification-error measures.
record.gate_note: The study reports training stability and collapse in deep diffusion Transformers, but not training classification error. Its FID/IS, image-generation, timestep-probe, and implementation-speed results do not measure the claim’s predicted training classification behavior. Prior-work results in Related Work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures collapse and stabilization in residual diffusion Transformers. It does not test any stated version: there are no classification-error results, teacher–student minima experiments, plain-versus-residual comparisons, activation-matched initialization tests, learning-rate stability thresholds, or batch-normalization comparisons. Squared flow-matching loss alone does not test V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors identify mean-dominated collapse in the studied ultra-deep diffusion Transformers. MV-Split prevents collapse and gives the best stable convergence/quality frontier among evaluated 400-layer protocols; a separate 1000-layer run demonstrates trainability over its measured horizon.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Post-Norm single-stream diffusion Transformers trained with rectified-flow generation loss, not the classification-training recipes in the versions. Main comparisons vary residual stabilization; the 1000-layer run has a separate training and post-training pipeline.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome changes with residual stabilization, learning rate, writer initialization, and whether MV-Split protects both attention and FFN branches. Lower learning rate delays baseline failure; standard initialization presents collapse progressively across depth rather than as delayed MMS.

fits_no_version.finding: Both unstabilized 400-layer baselines collapse; halving the learning rate delays failure. LayerScale and MV-Split remain stable over the measured horizon. A separate 1000-layer MV-Split run remains trainable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual-subspace control can stabilize the tested ultra-deep Post-Norm diffusion Transformers; MV-Split preserves faster convergence than the evaluated stable LayerScale control.

fits_no_version.finding: The Gaussian-initialized 128-layer control develops an early depth-wise collapse front and high loss plateau. Attention-only MV-Split at 1000 layers leaves an FFN-dominated failure pathway.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In these DiTs, standard writer initialization does not prevent mean-dominated collapse, and protecting only attention residual branches is insufficient.

record.problems: The evidence concerns generative diffusion objectives rather than classification error. The 1000-layer run uses a separate data and post-training pipeline and is not a matched comparison. The standard-initialization control is explicitly not a matched convergence comparison. Several diagnostics are figure-based, and the paper reports no uncertainty for the main stability outcomes.
record.rows_left_out: No training-classification-error results are reported. FID/IS values in Table 1 and timestep probe results in Appendix H measure generation quality and timestep decodability, not the claim’s predicted training classification error; excluded. Figure-only gradient and representation diagnostics are not needed to record the principal training-stability outcomes.

untested.parts: All parts: CIFAR training classification error, random or corrupted labels, capacity, and training-recipe qualifications.
All parts: two-layer ReLU teacher–student optimization, spurious minima frequency, and extra student neurons.
All parts: depth degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks, identity-shortcut comparisons, deep plain tanh initialization, and Fixup training without normalization.

All parts: activation-matched signal-preserving initializations, controlled learning-speed and trainable-depth comparisons, orthogonal versus Gaussian tanh weights, and orthogonal convolution kernels.
All parts: recovery above the initial linearized stability limit, curvature reduction, sharpness at the full-batch stability threshold, and divergence relative to that threshold.
All parts: batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and matched Fixup comparisons without normalization.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T3 classification conflicts with its correctly unlinked rows. The exclusion rests on the specific interventions, architectures, and outcomes named by the versions; classification error is not required by every version. Appendix J adds related negative controls, but none tests V1–V6.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR classification error, label corruption, optimizer comparisons, model size effects on classification error, and early stopping.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima frequency, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain batch-normalized convolutional classification networks, identity shortcuts, and their training-error comparison.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons, plain tanh depth, and orthogonal convolutional kernels.
Squared-loss learning-rate stability thresholds, sharpness, and edge-of-stability behavior.
Batch-normalization speed and learning-rate tolerance comparisons on MNIST, CIFAR-10, or ImageNet classification.

rows.subject: DiT-400Layer-Baseline
rows.operation_detail: Unstabilized Post-Norm baseline training; default learning rate.
rows.note: The reported outcome concerns diffusion training stability, not classification error.
rows.check: Divergence before the first checkpoint is correctly reported, but it measures none of V1–V6; 'absent' would incorrectly imply a tested claim effect was absent.

rows.subject: DiT-400Layer-Baseline (η/2)
rows.operation_detail: Unstabilized Post-Norm baseline training at half the default learning rate.
rows.value: diverges later in training; shown only as a pre-crash speed reference
rows.note: The lower learning rate delays failure but does not remove it.
rows.check: Lowering the learning rate delays collapse, but no initial linearized stability limit or sharpness threshold is measured. This cannot establish absence of V5.

rows.subject: DiT-400Layer-LayerScale
rows.baseline: unstabilized baselines enter the mean-dominated failure state
rows.note: Authors state LayerScale remains stable over the measured horizon, while its centered updates are also reduced.
rows.check: LayerScale stability measures none of the versions. Table 1 reports the best stable member of an initialization-gain sweep, rather than an unspecified single LayerScale configuration.

rows.subject: DiT-400Layer-MVSplit
rows.baseline: un-stabilized Post-Norm baseline and LayerScale controls
rows.value: removes collapse events; remains non-divergent over the measured horizon
rows.note: Matched 400-layer comparison; the text says MV-Split is substantially ahead of LayerScale by 20k–30k steps.
rows.check: MV-Split stability is a result for the study's residual method, not a test of a stated version. LayerScale also remains stable; the comparison with LayerScale concerns convergence and generation quality. Residual initialization protocols differ across methods.

rows.subject: DiT-1000Layer-MVSplit
rows.operation_detail: Separate scale-validation run using MV-Split residuals.

conditions.value: ImageNet pretraining, then separate ∼50k curated image set
measured horizon; full-horizon curve extends through 110k steps

rows.value: remains stable over the measured training horizon
rows.note: Separate pipeline; not a matched frontier comparison with the 400-layer controls.
rows.check: The separate 1000-layer run demonstrates trainability under MV-Split but tests none of the versions. Its different pipeline prevents a controlled depth comparison with the 400-layer runs.

rows.subject: DiT-128-layer standard-initialization control
rows.operation_detail: Training without residual gating, with Gaussian initialization for residual writers and final projection.
rows.baseline: zero-writer training runs described in the main text
rows.value: loss quickly reaches a high plateau; deep layers show high token similarity from the beginning and a depth-wise collapse front
rows.note: The paper says this is not a matched convergence comparison; it tests whether the state is specific to identity-start writers.
rows.check: Correct the Gaussian initialization notation to N(0, 0.02²). The 128-layer control is explicitly not a matched convergence comparison and does not test activation-matched initialization or any other version.

rows.subject: 1000-layer attention-branch-only MV-Split configuration
rows.operation_detail: Apply MV-Split only to the attention output residual branch; leave the FFN branch unchanged.
rows.baseline: full MV-Split protects both attention and FFN branches
rows.value: training still spikes at Step 7415 (Global Norm ≈ 0.665); FFN_W2 accounts for 14 of the top 15 contributors and about 93% of top-K squared-norm mass
rows.uncertainty: Per-rank loss standard deviation σ ∈ [0.011, 0.023] over the reported escalation; loss rises from ∼0.81 to ∼2.12
rows.note: This is an explicit branch-level negative control; the paper concludes attention-only control is insufficient.
rows.check: The spike and subsequent loss rise establish failure of attention-only MV-Split in this configuration, not absence of any V1–V6 effect.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
